name: Graphic Communication
strapline: Make ideas clear. Make design matter.
intro: Communicate technical information accurately and visual messages convincingly. Suggested BGE projects explore drawing, digital design and responsible communication. They are not confirmed school units. Senior Phase combines technical accuracy with visual impact; software is a tool, not the learning goal. Original practice tasks must not be submitted as live assessed assignments.

bge.title: Draw it so someone can make it
bge.question: Why are several views useful?
bge.task: Sketch a simple storage block from the front, top and side. Align corresponding features.
bge.extend: Explain which hidden detail cannot be understood from a single photograph.

bge.title: Messages that work
bge.question: How does layout guide a reader?
bge.task: Create a school-event poster using three levels of information and explain the reading order.
bge.extend: Test whether the message remains understandable in greyscale.

bge.title: From sketch to model
bge.question: How can a model improve an idea?
bge.task: Plan a simple phone stand on paper or approved CAD software, recording dimensions and assumptions.
bge.extend: Explain a modelling limitation such as material flexibility.

bge.title: Data with integrity
bge.question: Can a graphic mislead?
bge.task: Redesign a distorted bar chart with a zero baseline and clear source information.
bge.extend: Compare the effect of changing scale with changing the underlying data.

senior.title: National 4 Graphic Communication
senior.explain: Develop manual and digital communication skills through familiar and straightforward tasks.
senior.assessment: Internally assessed units and added-value assignment; pass/fail.

senior.title: National 5 Graphic Communication
senior.explain: Apply drawing conventions, CAD, colour, layout and presentation to communicate to a defined audience.
senior.assessment: Question paper and assignment. Teacher supervision and national conditions apply.

senior.title: Higher Graphic Communication
senior.explain: Handle more complex technical graphics and promotional communication, justifying design decisions.
senior.assessment: Question paper and assignment; use the current official task and specification.

skills.title: Orthographic accuracy
skills.explain: Aligned views describe the same object from different directions.
skills.try: Check that a hole has matching position in adjacent views.
skills.check: Corresponding widths, heights and depths agree; hidden detail uses the appropriate convention.

skills.title: Scale and dimensions
skills.explain: A drawing scale changes representation, not the real object.
skills.check: Its drawn length is 60 mm; its dimension label still gives the real 120 mm.

skills.title: Visual hierarchy
skills.explain: Size, placement, contrast and spacing guide attention.
skills.try: Identify the first three things a reader notices in a poster.
skills.check: The order should match the communication purpose and remain legible.

skills.title: Evaluate a CAD model
skills.explain: A successful model satisfies the brief and supports later communication.
skills.try: Review feature order and dimensions in a supplied model.
skills.check: Explain how an edit could affect dependent features rather than merely naming commands.

practice.question: A product is 80 mm wide. How wide should it appear at scale 2:1, and what dimension should be written?
practice.hint: Separate drawing size from actual size.
practice.answer: Draw it 160 mm wide, but label the real width as 80 mm. A dimension communicates the object, not the enlarged paper measurement.

practice.question: A poster uses pale yellow text on white, four decorative fonts and equal-sized headings. Suggest two justified improvements.
practice.hint: Connect decisions to readability and hierarchy.
practice.answer: Increase text-background contrast and establish a limited, consistent type hierarchy. This improves legibility and helps the reader find the main message before details.
practice.extend: Test the redesign on an iPad at normal viewing size.

practice.question: Why can a photorealistic rendered image fail to communicate manufacturing information?
practice.answer: A render can show appearance but may omit exact dimensions, hidden details, tolerances and technical conventions. Add appropriate technical drawings rather than assuming realism guarantees accuracy.
practice.extend: Identify a case where a render is still the most useful communication.

resources.title: V&A learning
resources.task: Choose a designed object and explain how form communicates its purpose.

resources.title: Design Museum learning
resources.task: Study a design story and identify user, need, constraint and response.

resources.title: Autodesk education
resources.task: Explore a teacher-selected CAD tutorial. School access and software arrangements may be required.

resources.title: Official past papers
resources.task: Choose a drawing interpretation question and check dimensions carefully.

resources.title: Understanding Standards
resources.task: Review published Graphic Communication examples with your teacher and discuss evidence of quality.

ipad.title: Design iteration
steps: Annotate three changes linked to the brief.
Save a second version with a short comparison.

ipad.title: Technical explainer
steps: Highlight aligned features across three views.
Record a captioned explanation of one hidden detail.
ipad.evidence: An annotated interpretation, with the original source acknowledged.

ipad.title: Accessibility audit
steps: Open your poster on an iPad.
Check text size, contrast and reading order.
Ask a peer to locate key information and record revisions.
ipad.evidence: A before-and-after layout with evidence of testing.

careers.nextStep: Explore college CAD and engineering technician routes.

careers.linkToLearning: Technical communication links design intent to building information.
careers.nextStep: Compare college and university architectural technology pathways.

careers.title: Graphic designer
careers.linkToLearning: Hierarchy, typography and audience awareness create visual messages.
careers.nextStep: Build a process portfolio and investigate college design courses.

careers.title: Product designer

careers.nextStep: Compare design apprenticeships where available and university product design entry requirements.

parentTip: Ask your young person to explain who a graphic is for and what the audience must understand. Discuss improvements to their own designs without doing the design for them.

visual.title: One object, two views
visual.question: A rectangular block is 40 mm wide, 30 mm high and 20 mm deep. Which dimensions are shown in the front elevation and in the plan?
visual.answer: Front elevation: width 40 mm and height 30 mm. Plan: width 40 mm and depth 20 mm. Orthographic views describe the same object from different directions.
